title: People Ops Handbook: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guidance
author: Elena Martinez
body:
Purpose and audience

This handbook codifies Redwood Inference's People Operations standards for hiring, employee onboarding, continuous performance and feedback, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, recruiters, and engineering and product leaders running interview loops, onboarding new teammates, and conducting performance conversations.

High-level principles

- Candidate experience: fast, transparent, and equitable.
- Onboarding: make new hires productive and connected within 90 days.
- Performance: continuous feedback with defensible, calibrated formal reviews.
- Managers: empowered with templates and clear escalation paths for performance or conduct issues.

Quick references

- Job requisition template: /confluence/hr/job-requisition-template
- Interview scorecard: /confluence/hr/interview-scorecard
- Offer letter templates: /confluence/hr/offer-letters
- 30/60/90 template: /confluence/hr/30-60-90-template
- 1:1 agenda template: /confluence/hr/1-1-template

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Overview: Aim for a balanced process that emphasizes quality, speed, and fairness. Target time-to-offer for IC roles is 4-6 weeks from requisition approval.

Requisition and approval steps

- Manager prepares job requisition using the canonical template. Required fields: role summary, core responsibilities, success metrics for 6/12 months, compensation band, interview loop, and hiring rationale.
- Submit requisition to People Ops for headcount and comp-band approval. People Ops SLA: 3 business days.
- Once approved, Recruiting posts the role and begins active sourcing.

Sourcing and screening

- Preferred channels: employee referrals, diversity partners, targeted outreach, and marketplaces.
- Recruiter phone screen: 30 minutes to cover motivation, basic skills, and compensation expectations. Use the interview-scorecard during screens.

Interview loop design

- Typical IC loop: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager screen -> Technical interview(s) -> Systems/collaboration exercise -> Manager/culture interview -> Final calibration/bar-raiser.
- Interviewers must record evidence on the scorecard, provide a numeric rating (1-5), and state a hiring recommendation.
- All interviewers must complete unconscious bias training and use the question bank to ensure consistency.

Decisioning and offers

- Debrief: hiring manager convenes a debrief within 48 hours of the final interview. Recruiter prepares summary and consolidated scorecard.
- Hiring rule of thumb: move to offer when >=75% of competencies are evaluated as sufficient and there are no unresolved red flags.
- Compensation approvals: offers above band require director approval; offers >20% above band require VP and People Ops approval.
- Offer timing: verbal offer within 1 business day after decision; written offer within 2 business days.

Background checks and pre-boarding

- Background and identity checks begin after verbal acceptance. For security-sensitive roles, additional clearance steps may be required.
- Pre-boarding checklist (owner: recruiter & manager): equipment order, calendar invites for week 1, Slack/email access, repo access requests, and benefits enrollment instructions.

2) Onboarding program and manager responsibilities

Principles: clarity, connection, and enablement. Onboarding is co-owned by People Ops (policy, benefits, compliance) and Hiring Manager (role training and day-to-day integration).

Pre-boarding (2 weeks prior to start)

- People Ops: sends welcome packet, benefit enrollment instructions, payroll forms, and policy links.
- Manager: sends role-specific welcome message, first-week agenda, schedules introductions, and assigns a buddy.

First day sample agenda

1. Welcome with manager (30 minutes)
2. People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies) (60 minutes)
3. Team introductions and lunch (60-90 minutes)
4. Tools and account provisioning with buddy (60 minutes)
5. First-day admin: SSO, 2FA, access requests, and dev environment checklist.

30/60/90 milestone framework

- 30 days: complete mandatory training, learn core systems, contribute to an introductory task, and have weekly 1:1s.
- 60 days: own a discrete feature or responsibility, demonstrate independent contributions, and get mid-onboarding feedback.
- 90 days: meet expectations for level; manager and People Ops calibrate goals and career development plan.

Manager checklist for the first 90 days

- Week 0: set clear success metrics, share org chart and team priorities, and identify key stakeholders.
- Weekly 1:1s with structured agenda (wins, priorities, blockers, development).
- Checkpoints at 30/60/90: provide documented feedback, update training plan, and confirm role alignment.

3) Performance and feedback cycles

Purpose: Foster continuous learning and produce reliable, calibrated outcomes for promotion and compensation decisions.

Continuous feedback expectations

- Managers must give regular feedback in 1:1s and after major milestones; material feedback should be entered into the People Ops performance system.
- Encourage upward feedback and peer feedback channels.

Formal review schedule

- Mid-year check-in (June) and year-end review (December). Managers submit reviews by published deadlines; calibration follows review submission.
- Promotion windows align with the formal cycles. Promotion packets should include project outcomes, peer feedback, and metrics of impact.

Calibration process

- Panels consist of managers, a People Ops partner, and a senior cross-functional reviewer. Calibration compares outcomes against the leveling rubric and documents rationale.
- Document calibration notes in the People Ops system for auditability.

Performance improvement and PIP process

- Start with informal coaching: document expectations, provide resources, and set short-term checkpoints (typically 30 days).
- Engage People Ops before initiating a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). PIPs should be measurable, time-bound (usually 60-90 days), and include clear success criteria and support resources.
- If a PIP fails, follow the separation checklist with Legal and People Ops sign-off.

4) Manager guidance: hiring, coaching, and difficult conversations

Inclusive hiring practices

- Create diverse interview panels and brief interviewers on the role's success criteria before interviewing.
- Use structured behavioral questions and require evidence for ratings.

Running effective 1:1s and development conversations

- Cadence: weekly for new hires (first 3 months), then minimum bi-weekly.
- 1:1 agenda template: wins, priorities, blockers, skill development, and feedback for manager.
- Feedback model: Situation -> Behavior -> Impact -> Next steps. Keep feedback specific, timely, and actionable.

Difficult conversations and separations

- Consult People Ops and Legal early for serious conduct or performance issues.
- Follow the documented separation workflow and obtain necessary approvals prior to formal termination.

5) Policies, approvals, and exceptions

Time off and flexible work

- PTO: accrue per policy; managers approve standard requests. Extended leaves require People Ops coordination.
- Remote/hybrid norms: teams set core hours and onsite expectations; managers must document team norms in the team wiki.

Compensation exceptions

- Approvals: offers above band need director approval; >20% above band requires VP and People Ops sign-off. Signing bonuses and relocation packages require Finance and People Ops approval.

Recordkeeping and retention

- Store interview scorecards, decision notes, and offer documentation in the People Ops hiring folder.
- Performance records (reviews, calibration notes, PIPs) are stored in the People Ops performance system with restricted access.

6) Templates and appendices (available as linked pages)

- Job requisition checklist, interview scorecard, 30/60/90 template, 1:1 agenda, offer letter samples, PIP template, and manager coaching checklist.

7) Roles and owners

- Hiring Manager: role definition, interview coordination, hiring recommendation, onboarding owner.
- Recruiting: sourcing, initial screens, and candidate experience owner.
- People Ops: policy ownership, compensation approvals, performance program management, and escalation partner.
- IT/Facilities: equipment procurement and workspace setup.

8) SLAs and common timelines

- Req approval: 3 business days (People Ops).
- Recruiter screen to first onsite: 7 business days (Recruiting).
- Offer after decision: 1 business day verbal, 2 business days written (Hiring Manager / Recruiting).
- New hire laptop provisioned: 5 business days before start (IT).

Change history

- 2025-03-05: Handbook created (Elena Martinez).
- 2025-09-15: Updated sourcing guidance and interviewer training requirements (Jordan Lee).
- 2026-03-01: Revised onboarding checklist and clarified PIP escalation (Maya Thompson).
